prose.summary: The aluminium windows meet the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED. Refer to the claim checklist below for the required steps.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, described as doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha’s confidence in this classification is medium, so you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India‑UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%, which applies only to Basic Customs Duty. Other import charges such as IGST are still payable. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and a value addition (VA) of at least 45%. CTSH means each non‑originating input must be classified in a different 6‑digit subheading, while VA is the share of the product’s price that does not come from non‑originating materials. The final manufacturing step was performed in the UAE and the work goes beyond the minimal operations listed in the agreement, so those checks are satisfied. All three non‑originating inputs are classified outside subheading 761010, fulfilling CTSH, and the value addition on an Ex‑Works basis is 43.0%, which exceeds the required 40% after the 5‑point reduction for Ex‑Works.

notes.text: The HS code provided (76101090) does not match any tariff line exactly; the closest match is 76101000. You should confirm the correct code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.

Preferential treatment applies only if the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control and without any operations other than unloading, reloading or storage. If a third party issues the invoice, you must indicate 'third‑party invoicing' on the certificate.
The given HS code 76101090 has no exact match; the candidate tariff line 76101000 is under the same 6-digit code. 8-digit codes are national and differ between the UAE and India.

The duty estimate is based on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement. The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A product that only undergoes the minimal operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q) does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.

Preference is given only to originating goods shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. An invoice issued by a third party does not by itself cause the claim to be denied; the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

Only for a certificate issued retrospectively: the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found). Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
The certificate does not remove the importer's duty of reasonable care, so the UAE exporter may be asked for production and cost details.
